set.body:
Problem
The current sparse k = 2 relation cost is normalized by total coupling mass. Under perfect reversal its residual falls approximately as 1/n as fixation count grows, so longer reversed paths can appear increasingly acceptable.

Implementation
Define a bounded edge-conditioned residual from the normalized coupling Gamma. Use a soft directed-Dice form r_T = 1 - 2C/(A+B+delta), where C is transported agreement between directed local edges and A/B normalize the supported source and target edge mass. Retain an ordinal local clock as the memory default; physical time remains an explicit alternative.

Acceptance criteria
- Identical local order yields residual near 0 and exact reversal near 1 on deterministic fixtures.
- Reversal values over n = 4, 8, 16, 32, and 64 remain within a prespecified 0.05 absolute band rather than decaying with n.
- Uniform temporal dilation does not change the ordinal-clock result.
- Local swaps, block reordering, and complete shuffle degrade in prespecified order at fixed coordinates and density.
- Zero-edge, one-fixation, two-fixation, duplicate-location, and coalesced-fixation cases are finite and documented.
- Proportional fixation splitting/merging is invariant after the declared coalescing or interval representation.
- The implementation uses matrix products, not explicit m^2 n^2 quadruple allocation, and has analytic plus metamorphic tests.
set.title: GW-18.2 Replace diluted chronology with an edge-normalized local-order residual
